why: The core habit: when a teammate drives, move to where they can see you.
say: Driver attacks the gap — shooter, don't stand and watch, slide to open space.
how: Ball at the top, shooter on the wing.
Driver attacks the gap between the top and wing.
Shooter drifts to the corner as the drive comes.
Kick out, catch ready, shoot. Switch spots.
cue: Shooter moves on the driver's 2nd dribble
h: Coach as help defender — driver scores if coach doesn't help.

st: Drive the gap — wing drifts to the corner

why: Teaches every player where to go on every drive.
say: On a drive: corners drift, the next player fills behind, and if the drive comes at you, lift.
how: 4-out: two slots, two corners. No defense.
Drive middle: corners drift down, opposite slot fills the top behind the driver.
Drive toward a corner: that corner lifts to the wing.
Driver kicks and relocates to the open spot. Keep it going for 60 seconds.
cue: Drift = slide away, stay in vision
Lift = drive comes at you, rise up
Fill = take the spot behind the driver
e: Coach calls the drive and freezes after each one.

st: Middle drive — corners drift, 2 fills behind
Drive at the corner — 4 lifts, 1 fills the top

why: Builds the 'good shot to great shot' extra pass.
say: Drive, kick, and if the closeout comes hard — swing it one more.
how: Top, wing, and corner spots; coach is the closeout defender.
Top drives the gap, kicks to the wing.
Coach closes out hard on the wing.
Wing makes the extra pass to the corner — shoot.
h: Coach chooses: close out or stay home. Wing reads it.

why: Attack a closeout, draw the help, and find the open teammate.
say: Beat the closeout, make the defender pick — if he stops you, pass.
how: Defender under the rim passes to a wing, closes out.
Wing drives past the closeout.
Opposite wing relocates along the baseline.
Read: score, or kick to the open teammate.
cue: Get two feet in the paint
Teammate moves into the driver's vision
e: Defender closes out at half speed.
h: Add a second defender who starts late (2-on-1 → 2-on-2).

why: Bigs relocate on drives too — easy dump-off layups.
say: Big, when the guard drives baseline, slide to the dunker spot on the other side.
how: Guard on the wing, big on the block with a defender.
Guard drives baseline.
Big slides to the opposite dunker spot; big's defender helps.
Dump-off pass, finish.
cue: Driver: two hands, bounce or flip
h: Defender chooses: help or stay — driver reads it.

st: Baseline drive — big slides to the dunker spot

say: No shot until the ball touches the paint — drive or post it first.
how: 4-on-4 or 5-on-5 half court.
The ball must touch the paint (drive or post catch) before any shot.
Bonus point for a kick-out three.
e: Paint touch only required on the first possession.
h: Paint touch must be a drive (no post entries).

st: Paint touch — help comes, corner drifts

why: Defense is a player short — offense must find the open player with drives and passes.
say: You're up one — penetrate, make them help, and find the open player.
how: 4 offense on the perimeter, 3 defenders.
Offense drives and kicks until someone is wide open.
Score = open shot. Rotate a new defender in.
h: Defense earns a point for each stop.

why: Dribble toward a denied teammate is the signal to cut backdoor.
say: If I dribble at you and you're denied, go backdoor right away.
how: Ball at the top, wing denied by a defender.
Ball handler dribbles at the wing.
Wing cuts backdoor; bounce pass; layup.

why: Keeps spacing alive: everyone rotates toward the space the driver left.
say: When someone drives, everyone rotates one spot toward the hole they left.
how: 5-out spacing.
Drive from the top: the wing on the drive side rotates up to the top, the corner lifts.
Driver kicks and fills the open corner.
Next drive goes the other way; keep rotating.

st: Drive right — everyone rotates toward the hole
Kick to the top — driver fills the corner

why: Baseline drives need a different read: trailer behind, skip to the far corner.
say: Baseline drive: top player trails behind for the pitch, far wing drops to the corner.
how: Players at both wings and the top.
Wing drives baseline.
Top trails behind the drive; far wing drops to the corner.
Driver reads: pitch back to the trailer or skip to the corner.
cue: Corner: be ready before the pass
e: Driver only passes to the corner.
h: Coach as help — driver reads where help comes from.

st: Baseline drive — top trails, far wing drops

why: Catch on a closeout and attack again — the defense never resets.
say: Catch on the kick, attack the closeout right away, then kick again.
how: Top, wing, and corner.
Top drives, kicks to the wing, relocates.
Wing drives baseline immediately; corner lifts.
Kick to the lift; shoot.
h: Add two defenders who close out.

why: Live game that rewards driving, relocating, and passing.
say: Every drive must end in a score or a kick — kick-out threes count double.
how: 3-on-3 half court.
Drives must end in a layup or a pass out (no picking it up in the lane).
Kick-out threes count double; first to 7.
e: Kick-out shots inside the arc count double.

why: Decide in half a second: drive to score, relocate, and keep the ball moving.
say: Drive to score and get your feet in the paint before you pass — receiver, HUNT a new spot.
how: Two lines at elbow-extended (both slots), one ball. Run at 2 hoops.
Start with a middle drive; driver must get feet in the paint before passing.
Receiver must lift or drift to a new spot (HUNT).
Catch and go right away — the whole team counts every pass.
Rounds: Rip & Go to 25, Jab & Go to 25, Shot Fake + Go to 25.
cue: Feet in the paint before the pass
Receiver: lift or drift, never stand
h: Add one help defender in the lane.

st: Middle drive, feet in the paint — receiver drifts (HUNT)
Rip & go — driver relocates to a new spot

why: Three motion reads off one flash: cut, screen away, or follow for a ball screen.
say: Flash to the top for the catch, reverse it, then run the option I call.
how: Two lines at the wings; ball in the left line.
Right-wing player flashes to the top and gets the pass.
Reverse the ball to the next wing, then run the called option:
1) Cut to the hoop  2) Screen away  3) Pass and follow for a ball screen.
cue: Option 2: screen the defender's spot, then roll
h: Add defense on the flash player; offense picks the option.
